messages:
ana: quick heads-up — after enabling KV prefill for low-latency tails we started hitting fragmentation-induced OOMs on some p4d machines. profiling shows lots of small live allocations + large freed gaps. see perf dashboard: https://perf.internal/r/kv-prefill-1815 :grimacing:

mike: ugh. did we change allocator flags with the prefill patch?

ana: (typo: ana) i ran heap profile while repro-ing:
```
GPU allocs: many small (<=256B) + steady 16MB prefill buffers
free map: dozens of ~512KB-4MB holes
OOM at 14.7GB/16GB
```

sanjay: that pattern screams fragmentation. prefill creates contiguous large buffers early, then per-request decode allocs fragment them when freed.

elaine: can you paste the prefill config?

ana: config snippet we used on canary:
```
kv_prefill_enabled: true
kv_prefill_target_mb: 200
kv_prefill_chunk_size_kb: 1024
per_request_kv_cap: 64
buffer_pool: disabled
small_alloc_threshold_bytes: 256
```

mike: two quick levers: 1) enable a slab/arena for small allocs (<=4KB) 2) switch prefill to many small chunks instead of few big ones. fragmentation tradeoff.

sanjay: +1. Also consider per-request decode-on-demand fallback for requests that would push workspace over threshold. i.e. if (workspace_free < X) then decode not prefill.

elaine: how about reuse: pool big prefill buffers and always allocate per-request from pool instead of freeing to global allocator? that reduces holes.

ana: did a quick sim: splitting 200MB prefill into 512KB chunks reduced max hole size by ~10x in the trace and avoided the OOM. small alloc slab reduced peak virtual allocs by about 8%.

mike: nice. we should also tune kernel selection — some kernels allocate temporary buffers differently; those temporaries are contributing to fragmentation during long batched decode. we saw kernels A and C have larger transient allocations.

sanjay: can we add a cheap heuristic: adaptive-evict — when prefill + live_temp > threshold, evict least-recently-used KV segments below per-request cap until under threshold. avoids hard OOM and preserves hot items.

elaine: proposal for experiments (short):
1) enable small-slab allocator for <=4KB (canary)
2) prefill chunk size = 512KB, keep target 200MB
3) per_request_kv_cap = 32 (hard cap) + eviction debounce 100ms
4) enable buffer_pool for prefill buffers
measure: OOM counts, fragmentation metric (largest_free_block/total_free), p95 latency, kernel memory high-water.

mike: add one more: record per-kernel transient allocation histogram to correlate kernel selection with fragmentation events.

deploy-bot: canary rollout started for kevin/kv-prefill-slab-512 @ 1815002000 (5 hosts). Monitor /ops/kv-prefill-canary.

ana: i'll run the experiment and post profiles. if results good we'll roll to all p4d with gradual throttle.

elaine: if we still see fragmentation, fallback is to keep prefill but use per-host per-model pinned arenas and compact occasionally (triggered during low-traffic windows). compaction is expensive though.

sanjay: agree on compaction as last resort. prefer pool + chunking + per-request caps + eviction heuristics.

mike: thanks. prioritize slab allocator + prefill chunking first. please include a small patch to kernel alloc accounting so we can attribute temporary allocs to kernels in the next run.

ana: noted — will open a PR for slab + chunking + perf hooks. posting results later today. :thumbsup:
